assignment: 卷之六 古今富貴貧賤嬭壽命圖 — the worked-nativity gallery of the Ming Nanyangtang seven-juan printing; scan leaves ~187-255
juan_boundaries_observed: 版心 montage over leaves 24-264 places 卷之一 at leaves 4-33, 卷之二 34-56, 卷之三 57-116, 卷之四 117-155, 卷之五 156-186, 卷之六 187-255, 卷之七 256-265. Leaf 200 fold reads 紫微斗數全書 / 卷之六.
notes: MAJOR CORRECTION TO THE TRACK. The corpus defensibility spec states, on the strength of a three-juan Wikisource transcription, that 'a dated worked nativity - none printed anywhere in the work' and marks it refused. That is false for this seven-juan Ming printing: 卷之六 is a gallery of dozens of fully worked nativities, two per leaf-spread, each carrying a named subject, a sexagenary birth year, lunar month, lunar day and double-hour, the polarity/sex label (陰男 / 陽女 etc.), the five-phase bureau as the compiler computed it, a complete twelve-palace star grid with the twelve-stage cycle marked in every palace, the 博士十二神 in every palace, 大限 and 小限 markers, a death record, and a judgment paragraph. Two charts have been independently recomputed here and BOTH reproduce the printed bureau, the printed life palace and the printed twelve-stage direction exactly from the birth data alone. The twelve-stage direction question the corpus records as source_gated is answered by these charts empirically: 陰男 runs the cycle in reverse.

subject.identification_note: 耿弇 (Geng Yan, 3-58 CE) was one of the Eastern Han founding generals of the Yuntai twenty-eight. The identification is the encoder's, from the printed name alone; the block gives no dynasty or office.

birth_record.chinese: 癸丑年三月初四辰時生
birth_record.engine_rendering: Born in the guichou year, third month, fourth day, chen double-hour.

death_or_outcome_record.chinese: 戊午年六十六歲五月初五故
death_or_outcome_record.engine_rendering: Died in the wuwu year, aged sixty-six, on the fifth day of the fifth month.
death_or_outcome_record.output_policy_reason: death-timing record; retained as a historical worked-example datum for engine validation, never rendered as a claim about any living person

palace_axis.body_palace_label_chinese: 身 (marked inside the 才帛 palace)
palace_axis.twelve_palaces_run: reverse branch order from the life palace, as the work's own 安十二宮例 prescribes

寅.reading_note: the 紫微/天府 pair sits at the foot of the bottom-row cell adjoining 田宅; the encoder assigns them to 寅 because the printed bureau 金四局 with lunar day 4 requires 紫微 at 寅 and the mirror rule then requires 天府 at 寅. Flagged as a reading, not a certainty.

conclusion.palace_grid_confidence: the twelve palace labels, the twelve-stage marks and the 博士十二神 are read with confidence; individual star-to-cell assignments in the upper half of each cell are read at 300ppi from a woodblock and a few are inferred from the cell boundary rather than seen isolated - each such case is noted in the cell

judgment_text.chinese: 破軍若在子午，官資清顯，至三公；又兼左右、昌曲加會，文武雙全富貴之命。大限到于天傷，有嫌巨門太歲，到午謂之沉馬，流羊當頭，小限冲太歲凶，故死。
judgment_text.engine_rendering: If Pojun stands at Zi or Wu, the office is pure and eminent, reaching the Three Dukes; and with Zuofu and Youbi joined, and Wenchang and Wenqu meeting it, civil and martial are both complete - a nativity of wealth and rank. When the decade limit came to Tianshang, with the disliked Jumen and the year-lord, and it reached Wu, which is called the sunken horse, the flowing Qingyang stood over the head and the small limit clashed with the year-lord: inauspicious, and therefore he died.
judgment_text.output_policy_reason: death-timing clause and a rank verdict on a person; retained verbatim as historical text and as the compiler's own stated judgment for validation, never rendered as a claim about any living person

engine_recomputation_check.performed_by: encoder, from the printed birth record alone, without reference to the printed answers
engine_recomputation_check.life_palace: month 3 counted from 寅 gives the month palace 辰; 辰 taken as the Zi hour and counted back to the 辰 hour gives 子 - matches the printed 命垣
engine_recomputation_check.body_palace: the same count taken forward gives 申 - matches the printed 身 mark inside 才帛
engine_recomputation_check.bureau: year stem 癸 under the Five Tigers rule starts 寅 at 甲寅, so the 子 palace carries the stem-branch 甲子, whose nayin is 海中金 - metal - giving 金四局, which is exactly what the block prints
engine_recomputation_check.ziwei: 金四局 with lunar day 4 gives 紫微 at 寅, and the mirror rule then gives 天府 at 寅; 廉貞 at 紫微+4 = 午 and 天相 at 午 both match the printed 遷移 cell
engine_recomputation_check.lucun: year stem 癸 gives 祿存 at 子 - matches the printed 命垣 cell
engine_recomputation_check.twelve_stage_direction: 金四局 sets 長生 at 巳; the printed stages run 巳長生 辰沐浴 卯冠帶 寅臨官 丑帝旺 子衰 亥病 戌死 酉墓 申絕 未胎 午養, i.e. REVERSE - which settles empirically that this witness runs the cycle backward for a 陰男
engine_recomputation_check.boshi_direction: 博士 at 祿存 (子) and the twelve gods run backward - 亥力士 戌青龍 酉小耗 申將軍 未奏書 午飛廉 巳喜神 辰病符 卯大耗 寅伏兵 丑官府 - matching every printed cell
engine_recomputation_check.verdict: every construction step the encoder could recompute reproduces the block. This chart is a genuine end-to-end validation vector for the bureau, the life and body palaces, Zi Wei placement, Lu Cun, the twelve-stage cycle and the twelve gods.

exceptions: The printed death record gives an age of sixty-six; the historical Geng Yan died in 58 CE at about fifty-six. The block's own figure is recorded as printed and is not reconciled with the historical record.
The subject identification is the encoder's, from a bare personal name; the block gives no dynasty, office or dates.

judgment_text.chinese: 雙祿朝垣，又兼巨机對宮相會，最善談兵。日月左右來宮加會，命垣應貴。大乙巳年二十五歲，太歲埋蛇，乙年太陰星化忌，故主凶亡。
judgment_text.engine_rendering: A double Lu facing the palace, and Jumen and Tianji in the opposite palace meeting it: best of all at discoursing on war. Sun and Moon with Zuofu and Youbi coming into the palace and joining, so the life palace ought to be noble. In the great yisi year, at twenty-five, the year-lord was the buried snake, and in a yi year the star Taiyin takes the Ji transformation - therefore an inauspicious death.
judgment_text.output_policy_reason: death-timing clause and a rank verdict on a person; retained verbatim as historical text and as the compiler's own stated judgment for validation, never rendered as a claim about any living person

extent.engine_rendering: Juan six of the seven-juan printing consists of this gallery and nothing else; the centre-fold montage places it at scan leaves 187 to 255, roughly sixty-nine leaf-spreads, with one full chart per half-page.

per_chart_form.chinese: 陰男 金四局 癸丑年三月初四辰時生
per_chart_form.engine_rendering: Each chart prints: a heading naming the subject; the polarity-and-sex label; the five-phase bureau; a sexagenary birth year with lunar month, lunar day and double-hour; a twelve-palace grid carrying the star placements, the twelve-stage cycle mark and the twelve-god mark for every palace, with the decade limit and small limit flagged; a death or outcome record; and a judgment paragraph running across the foot of the page.

correction_of_the_prior_finding.engine_rendering: The corpus's prior finding, taken from a three-juan Wikisource transcription, that this work prints no dated worked nativity is wrong for this witness. The transcription simply lacks juan six.

exceptions: The leaf-range figure 187-255 is derived from a centre-fold sampling montage at six-leaf intervals, not from leaf-by-leaf inspection; the true first and last leaf of the juan may differ by a few leaves.
